The shoulder joint connects the humeral head to the scapular socket. The four rotator cuff muscles and their tendons help stabilize and move the arm. The scapula and other muscles also contribute to raising the arm, pulling and pressing.

Shoulder pain can arise from different structures and conditions. Exercise names or pain location alone do not determine a diagnosis. Tears or tendon injuries need assessment based on history and examination.
The femur, tibia and patella form the knee joint. Articular cartilage supports movement, menisci help distribute load and ligaments stabilize the joint. Thigh muscles move the knee through tendons.

Menisci, ligaments and tendons are different structures. Swelling, locking or difficulty bearing weight require assessment. Choosing an adapted exercise does not replace identifying the cause of symptoms.
The spine: neck and lower back

The spine consists of vertebrae, discs, joints and ligaments, with muscles supporting movement. There are seven cervical and five lumbar vertebrae. Nerves pass through the canal and exit between vertebrae.
Pain and range-of-motion reports can help monitor change, but cannot identify a disc or nerve as the cause on their own. Your team sets return-to-activity pathways based on individual assessment.
RPE, RIR and e1RM in the app

RPE describes perceived set effort. On a reps-in-reserve scale, RPE 10 means no additional rep is possible, RPE 9 about one and RPE 8 about two. RIR is your estimate of additional possible reps. RIR 2 and RPE 8 are equivalent in the app's calculation. This self-assessment improves with experience.

Your coach sets RPE or RIR targets and you report actual effort. The app estimates e1RM from weight, reps and effort and may suggest next-set weight changes. Suggestions use equipment increments and a maximum 5% change, and are withheld when pain is reported. This mathematical estimate is not a maximal strength measurement, medical clearance or advice to attempt a maximal lift.

- One demonstration per exercise, with its name at the beginning.
- Landscape filming, stable camera, even lighting and a clear background. Keep body and equipment visible throughout.
- Film the starting position, controlled reps and ending position. Choose a demonstration load with the coach; do not present reps or weight as personal dosage.

- Add short captions from the recorded cues. The narration draft below requires professional review.
- Upload MP4 or WebM, up to 25 MB each. Keep a separate high-quality original.
- Before publishing, check playback, exercise match, captions, filming rights and absence of private client information.
